title: A redirected phase forms a round span
statement: Let $k,n\in\mathbb{N}$, let $x$ be a finite binary input, let $c$ be a configuration of a $k$-tape machine with states indexed by $\{0,\ldots,n\}$, and let $a$ be one of its actions. Choose a phase label $j$ other than the entry or halt label, configurations $d,e$ in that phase, and a time $T$. Suppose the phase machine runs from $d$ to $e$ in $T$ steps; the state of $e$ is $s$; the phase redirection at $(j,s)$ produces a next labelled phase; no state encountered at any time $u<T$ redirects; and the round-window property holds at every phase-machine time $u\le T$. Then the full round machine runs from $d$ embedded under label $j$ to $e$ embedded in the redirected next phase in $T+1$ steps, with the round-span property.
hypotheses_covered: Natural numbers $k,n$ and finite binary input $x$
Phase label differs from entry and halt
Configurations $d,e$ in the phase indexed by the label
Phase-machine run from $d$ to $e$ in $T$ steps
Redirection at $(j,s)$ equals the specified next labelled phase
No earlier phase state redirects at times $u<T$
Round-window property holds for all phase-machine times $u\le T$
